items.topic: MCP-level digit amputation versus ray resection
items.destination_intent: OITE hand teaching note canonical section for digit amputation and ray resection
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside the comparison of preserved palmar width/grip mechanics versus improved cosmesis, first webspace, and reduced residual-digit interference
items.caption_intent: MCP-level index-finger amputation preserves palmar width, whereas ray resection narrows the palm but may improve cosmesis, first-webspace function, and avoidance of a prominent metacarpal head.

items.destination_intent: OITE pathology teaching note canonical section for fibrous dysplasia and multifocal bone-lesion imaging differential
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside the comparison of ground-glass expansile lesions with Ollier disease, Paget disease, multiple myeloma, and hereditary multiple exostoses
items.caption_intent: Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia question showing multifocal, asymmetric ground-glass expansile lesions with cortical thinning.

items.topic: Imaging differential of multifocal bone lesions: polyostotic fibrous dysplasia
items.destination_intent: OITE pathology teaching note canonical section for fibrous dysplasia and multifocal bone-lesion imaging differential
items.teaching_point_placement: Immediately after the question image as its provided explanation and imaging discriminator summary
items.caption_intent: Provided explanation contrasting fibrous dysplasia with hereditary multiple exostoses, Ollier disease, Paget disease, and multiple myeloma.

items.destination_intent: OITE pathology teaching note canonical section for fibrous dysplasia and the multifocal bone-lesion imaging differential
items.teaching_point_placement: Within the side-by-side imaging comparison, first as the fibrous dysplasia example
diagnostic_features: Multifocal intramedullary lesions involving more than one bone
Hazy ground-glass to mixed lytic-sclerotic matrix rather than discrete punched-out defects
Smooth fusiform expansion and bowing with cortical thinning
Cortex remains largely intact without aggressive periosteal reaction or a surface-based exostosis
items.caption_intent: Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia: multifocal intramedullary ground-glass/mixed lesions produce smooth osseous expansion, bowing, and cortical thinning while preserving a relatively intact cortex; these features distinguish it from enchondromas, Paget disease, myeloma, and exostoses.

items.destination_intent: OITE pathology teaching note canonical section for enchondromas, Ollier disease, and the multifocal bone-lesion imaging differential
items.teaching_point_placement: Within the side-by-side imaging comparison, second as the Ollier disease example
diagnostic_features: Numerous central and eccentric intramedullary lucent lesions in phalanges, metacarpals, and distal forearms
Lobulated geographic morphology with cortical expansion and endosteal scalloping
Chondroid stippled or ring-and-arc mineralization in several lesions
Asymmetric burden with marked digital deformity, enlargement, and shortening
items.caption_intent: Ollier disease (multiple enchondromatosis): numerous asymmetric, lobulated intramedullary enchondromas expand and scallop the phalanges/metacarpals, contain chondroid stippled or ring-and-arc mineralization, and cause severe digital deformity.

items.destination_intent: OITE pathology teaching note canonical section for Paget disease and the multifocal bone-lesion imaging differential
items.teaching_point_placement: Within the side-by-side imaging comparison, third as the Paget disease example
diagnostic_features: Skull radiograph shows calvarial thickening with patchy cotton-wool sclerosis
Axial skull CT shows bone expansion, cortical thickening, widened diploic space, and irregular sclerosis
Pelvis demonstrates mixed lucency and sclerosis with coarse trabeculae and cortical thickening
Humerus shows enlargement and cortical/trabecular thickening; the pedigree supports familial clustering but is not itself an imaging criterion
items.caption_intent: Paget disease: skull radiograph/CT demonstrate calvarial expansion, thickened cortices and diploic space, and patchy cotton-wool sclerosis; pelvic and humeral films show mixed lytic-sclerotic remodeling, coarse trabeculae, and bone enlargement.

items.destination_intent: OITE pathology teaching note canonical section for multiple myeloma and the multifocal bone-lesion imaging differential
items.teaching_point_placement: Within the side-by-side imaging comparison, fourth as the multiple myeloma example
diagnostic_features: Panel a shows a sharply marginated punched-out lytic lesion in the glenoid without a mineralized matrix or reactive rim
Panels b and c localize metabolic activity on FDG-PET/CT and NaF-PET/CT
Panel d is STIR hyperintense and panel e is T1 hypointense, indicating marrow replacement
Panel f shows diffusion restriction with high DWI signal and panel g shows corresponding low ADC
items.caption_intent: Multiple myeloma: the glenoid lesion is a discrete punched-out lucency on radiograph; PET/CT shows metabolic activity, while MRI demonstrates T1-low, STIR-high marrow replacement with diffusion restriction (high DWI/low ADC).

items.destination_intent: OITE pathology teaching note canonical section for osteochondroma, hereditary multiple exostoses, and the multifocal bone-lesion imaging differential
items.teaching_point_placement: Within the side-by-side imaging comparison, fifth as the hereditary multiple exostoses example
diagnostic_features: Multiple surface-based exophytic osseous projections around the knee and elbow metaphyses
Sessile and pedunculated morphology with lesions projecting away from the adjacent joint or physis
Cortical and medullary continuity with the parent bone, diagnostic of osteochondroma
Surface origin distinguishes these lesions from the intramedullary enchondromas of Ollier disease
items.caption_intent: Hereditary multiple exostoses: multiple sessile/pedunculated metaphyseal osteochondromas project from the bone surface away from nearby joints and maintain cortical and medullary continuity with the parent bone.

items.diagnosis: Chronic throwing-related elbow UCL/MCL tear treated with reconstruction
items.destination_intent: OITE shoulder and elbow teaching note canonical section for throwing elbow UCL injury and reconstruction
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside the complication comparison for medial elbow UCL reconstruction
diagnostic_features: High-level overhead athlete with progressive medial elbow pain during pitching
Failed nonoperative treatment leading to UCL reconstruction
Transient ulnar nerve neuropraxia is the most common postoperative complication because the nerve lies directly behind the medial epicondyle and is manipulated during exposure
Modern muscle-splitting approaches avoid routine flexor-pronator detachment and routine ulnar nerve transposition
items.caption_intent: Throwing-related UCL injury treated with reconstruction: transient ulnar nerve neuropraxia is the most common complication; modern muscle-splitting techniques minimize flexor-pronator injury and avoid routine ulnar nerve transposition.

items.topic: Early Appropriate Care resuscitation thresholds before definitive fracture fixation
items.diagnosis: Adequately resuscitated polytrauma patient suitable for early definitive femoral and acetabular fixation
items.destination_intent: OITE trauma teaching note canonical section for damage-control orthopaedics versus Early Appropriate Care
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside the physiologic resuscitation criteria for proceeding with definitive fixation
diagnostic_features: Hemodynamically stable patient who is awake and conversant
Serum lactate 1.9 mmol/L indicates adequate resuscitation
Definitive fixation of the femoral shaft and acetabular fractures is favored over damage-control temporization
Early Appropriate Care uses lactate, pH, and base-excess/base-deficit thresholds rather than requiring complete normalization
items.caption_intent: Early Appropriate Care: a stable polytrauma patient with lactate 1.9 mmol/L is adequately resuscitated for early definitive femoral and acetabular fixation; do not delay solely to normalize lactate below 1.0.

items.topic: Proximal phalanx fracture malunion and PIP extensor lag
items.diagnosis: Transverse proximal phalanx fracture with apex-volar sagittal angulation
items.destination_intent: OITE hand teaching note canonical section for proximal phalanx fracture deforming forces and malunion consequences
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside the mechanism linking apex-volar malunion to loss of active PIP extension
diagnostic_features: AP alignment can appear acceptable while the lateral radiograph reveals sagittal-plane apex-volar angulation
Interossei flex the proximal fragment
The central slip/extensor mechanism pulls the distal fragment into extension
Persistent apex-volar malunion creates extensor-mechanism inefficiency and active PIP extension lag
items.caption_intent: Transverse proximal phalanx fracture: interossei flex the proximal fragment while the central slip extends the distal fragment, producing apex-volar angulation; healing in this position causes a predictable active PIP extensor lag.
